name: Lirac

limits: For white wine, Bourboulenc, Clairette, Grenache Blanc and Roussanne, each: at most 60%
For white wine, Marsanne, Piquepoul Blanc, Ugni Blanc and Viognier, each: at most 25%
For white wine, Marsanne, Piquepoul Blanc, Ugni Blanc and Viognier together: at most 30%
For red wine, Grenache: at least 40%
For red wine, Mourvèdre and Syrah together: at least 25%
For red wine, Carignan: at most 10%
For red wine, Clairette Rose, Counoise, Grenache Gris and Piquepoul Noir together: at most 10%
For rosé wine, Grenache: at least 40%
For rosé wine, Mourvèdre and Syrah together: at least 25%
For rosé wine, Carignan: at most 10%

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.

notes: Red Lirac often resembles a soft Côtes du Rhône Villages, while the more ambitious wines are closer to Châteauneuf-du-Pape.

blurb.text: A southern Rhône appellation in the Gard, on the right bank of the Rhône. It borders Tavel, and its wines use Grenache, Mourvèdre, Syrah and Cinsault for red, and Clairette and Grenache Blanc for white.
